newsitem.title: USA: Investors urge Woolworth to reinstate cash dividend.
newsitem.headline: Investors urge Woolworth to reinstate cash dividend.

text.p: A group led by Greenway Partners L.P., a New York-based investment firm, said Monday it submitted a proposal to Woolworth Corp. seeking to reinstate the retailer's cash dividend on common stock.

The group, which holds a 6 percent stake in Woolworth, said it submitted the proposal Jan. 3 for consideration by the company's shareholders at the retailer's next annual meeting scheduled to be held in June.
In making the proposal, the group said Woolworth had an 83-year tradition of paying cash dividends which ended in April 1995 when the dividend to holders of common stock was eliminated.
A copy of the proposed shareholder resolution was attached to a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission.

In battling for a resumption of the dividend, the group noted that "Woolworth today is a far stronger company." It said that "even a nominal one of 10 or 12 cents per quarter will show the market that the management of Woolworth has confidence in the strength of the turnaround."
In addition, the group said, reinstating the dividend "would increase the universe of potential purchasers of Woolworth common stock."

It said it continued to believe that Woolworth would do even better if its Foot Locker unit were spun off as a separate public company. The group had sponsored a resolution at last year's annual meeting seeking the spinoff.
The group said it holds 8.07 million Woolworth shares including its most recent purchase of 40,000 shares at $11.125 a share or $446,000.
